name: Self-healing subsea cable
subtitle: a sea cable that seals its own punctures

effects.effect: capsules in a plastic burst when it cracks and glue the crack shut
a one-atom sheet of carbon carries electrons extremely fast and blocks every gas

effect: capsules in a plastic burst when it cracks and glue the crack shut
how: A trawl net or a dragged anchor nicks a power or data cable, seawater creeps into the nick, and months later a continent loses a link that takes a repair ship weeks and millions to fix. The insulation holds capsules whose glue is squeezed out and cured by the very pressure of the deep water trying to get in, and a wrapped sheet of one-atom carbon, which no gas or water molecule can cross, backs up the seal.
obstacle: At four kilometres down the glue has to set and hold at four hundred atmospheres and near-freezing cold, where most resins never cure.
why: Uses the sea's own pressure, the thing that causes the failure, to drive the repair.
real: Prysmian's SUPERSEAL sells pressure-triggered self-healing sealant in cable insulation, but for low-voltage direct-burial cable, and SINTEF's microcapsule healing of electrical trees is only proposed for subsea connectors; no deep-water pressure-cured repair layer backed by a graphene barrier has been demonstrated.
